extracted.intended_audience: Royal Road fiction readers and writers (site users who leave ratings/reviews)
extracted.subtask_description: Discussing how to rate fiction on RoyalRoad and proposing improvements to the site's rating categories so they reflect what readers care about. Focuses on the mismatch between component scores (style/story/grammar/character) and an overall 'worth it' judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Style / Story / Grammar / Character component ratings
rubrics_metrics.description: Royal Road's existing component categories (style, story, grammar, character) used to rate parts of a fiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These component ratings are primarily useful to writers because they point to specific parts of the work to improve. They measure aspects like prose style, plot/structure, language correctness, and character development rather than a reader's overall judgement of whether the work was worth reading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall score should represent 'was it worth it'
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'Overall' rating ought to measure whether the experience of reading was worth the reader's time — a 'worth it' judgment — rather than being an aggregate of component scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author used the Overall score as a placeholder for 'worth it' because the existing categories don't capture that. Anti-pattern: giving an overall score that is inconsistent with component ratings (e.g., middling component scores but a perfect Overall).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency between component ratings and overall rating
rubrics_metrics.description: Ratings should not contradict each other — the overall rating should align with the component ratings or else be explicitly a different dimension (e.g., 'worth it').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example problem: wanting to 'rate everything middle-of-the-road but give the overall score a 5-star rating' which 'didn't make sense.' If Overall is used as a different concept, it should be labeled and explained to avoid confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate 'worth it' into meaningfulness and readability
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal to split the overall 'worth it' judgment into two reader-centered categories: meaningfulness (was the content good) and readability (was it easy to read).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meaningfulness = did the story/content feel meaningful to the reader; Readability = how easy/enjoyable it was to consume. This split would better capture what readers value than only component technical scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize different stakeholders' needs (writers vs readers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand that current rating categories serve writers (who want actionable feedback on elements) while readers care more about an overall enjoyment/meaningfulness metric.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design or interpret rating systems with the intended audience in mind: provide granular component feedback for creators, and provide summary 'worth it' metrics for consumers.
